candidate.title: Pseudo-seq
candidate.scope: The Pseudo-seq row of the assigned Illumina schematic: a poly(A)-selected RNA route through CMC-dependent RT truncation, cDNA size selection, circularization and PCR to a DNA library. Pseudouridine-residue drawings are target legends. Adjacent miCLIP-m6A, Ψ-seq/PSI-seq and ICE rows are contextual separate assays, not alternatives in this card. circLigase is a component, not an additional target method. This is the depicted Pseudo-seq implementation, not every input or protocol within the broader family.

states.label: Purified PCR-amplified cDNA-derived DNA library
features: The diagram endpoint is labelled cDNA after PCR and purify DNA; the sequenced material is DNA derived from RNA templates.
Transcript sequence identifies the RNA of origin; endpoint enrichment at CMC-dependent RT stops provides positional evidence for pseudouridines.
Interpreting Ψ requires distinguishing background RT stops; the paper uses matched −CMC libraries, although that control route is not depicted here.

In the primary readout, mapped read 5′ ends accumulate one nucleotide 3′ of Ψ in the +CMC library relative to its −CMC control. Downstream RT stops can shadow upstream Ψ sites, so absence of a peak does not establish absence of modification.

operations.label: Fragmentation and size selection
operations.description: The drawn combined block converts poly(A)-selected RNA into shorter RNA fragments and labels them size-selected before CMC. In the primary implementation, fragmentation precedes CMC, while RNA size selection follows CMC treatment and dephosphorylation; the graph retains the diagram grouping (c_rna_order).
operations.information_effect: Red pseudouridine site markers are retained within transcript fragments; the preparation limits the input population to poly(A)-selected RNA.

operations.label: CMC treatment and OH- treatment
operations.description: Chemically derivatizes RNA fragments and then reverses labile U/G modifications under alkaline conditions, leaving pseudouridine-associated CMC adducts that can block reverse transcription.
operations.mechanism: CMC modification followed by alkaline reversal of U/G modification; retained CMC–Ψ supplies an RT block.
operations.information_effect: Creates a chemical handle for positional detection without isolating every pseudouridine-bearing RNA molecule.

operations.label: Adaptor ligation
operations.description: Attaches a 3′ adapter to treated RNA fragments; green adapter segments appear on the RNA ends while CMC–Ψ sites remain.
operations.information_effect: Supplies the adapter interface used to initiate reverse transcription and carry the RNA fragment into a DNA library.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Copies adapter-bearing RNA into cDNA. CMC–Ψ can terminate extension, producing truncated cDNAs together with longer copying products.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcriptase is blocked one nucleotide 3′ to a CMC-modified pseudouridine, as specified by the primary paper.
operations.information_effect: Converts the RNA-site modification into a cDNA endpoint associated with transcript-derived sequence. Background RT stops mean that an endpoint alone is not a unique Ψ call.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and the third diagram row explicitly identify Pseudo-seq. The page-75 heading and matching circularization schematic verify the secondary-page match. Carlile et al. full text names Pseudo-seq and supports its CMC/RT/cDNA-circularization architecture. All seven operations belong to this single row; the early RNA-size-selection grouping differs from the primary order as recorded in c_rna_order. The paper also uses total-RNA inputs and −CMC controls, but those are not additional drawn routes in this scoped extraction.
